final_proof:
Proof. We use the inverse-image description of locale morphisms. For a locale L, write O(L) for its frame of opens. A point p of L is a frame homomorphism p: O(L) → 2. For a ∈ O(L), put U_a = {p ∈ Sp(L) : p(a) = 1}. These sets form the topology on Sp(L): preservation of finite meets and arbitrary joins by points gives U_{a ∧ b} = U_a ∩ U_b and U_{∨_i a_i} = ∪_i U_{a_i}. The component of the counit at L is the locale morphism σ_L: ΩSp(L) → L whose inverse-image frame homomorphism is σ_L^*: O(L) → O(Sp(L)), a ↦ U_a.

Let f: L → M be an arbitrary locale morphism, and denote its inverse-image frame homomorphism by f^*: O(M) → O(L). The spectrum map Sp(f): Sp(L) → Sp(M) sends a point p: O(L) → 2 to the point p ∘ f^*: O(M) → 2. For every b ∈ O(M), it consequently satisfies

Sp(f)^{-1}(U_b) = {p ∈ Sp(L) : (p ∘ f^*)(b) = 1} = U_{f^*(b)}.

We must prove that the naturality square commutes, namely

σ_M ∘ ΩSp(f) = f ∘ σ_L : ΩSp(L) → M.

Locale morphisms are equal if and only if their inverse-image frame homomorphisms are equal. Since inverse images reverse composition, for every b ∈ O(M) we have

(σ_M ∘ ΩSp(f))^*(b) = (ΩSp(f))^*(σ_M^*(b)) = Sp(f)^{-1}(U_b) = U_{f^*(b)},

whereas

(f ∘ σ_L)^*(b) = σ_L^*(f^*(b)) = U_{f^*(b)}.

Thus the two inverse-image homomorphisms agree on every element of O(M), so the two locale morphisms agree. As f was arbitrary, the family (σ_L)_L satisfies the naturality condition. Hence σ: ΩSp → id_Loc is a natural transformation. ∎
